en: The carabao, the Philippine national animal, is a domesticated swamp buffalo used by farmers to plow rice fields.
Sampaguita, the national flower, is a white jasmine species that blooms year-round and is woven into traditional Filipino garlands.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is a critically endangered raptor endemic to the forests of Mindanao and Luzon.
The Legislative branch of the Philippine government, composed of the Senate and House of Representatives, makes national laws.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of Luzon over 2,000 years ago using stone walls.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, with Filipino and English serving as the official languages for government and education.
Jose Rizal, the Philippine national hero, was an ophthalmologist who wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo.
The mango, specifically the Guimaras and Zambales varieties, is the national fruit of the Philippines and a major agricultural export.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a traditional dance stepping forward and backward to mimic a river current.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen at least eighteen years old has the right to vote in national elections.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for rural hospitals.
